keyframe_review.note: -404..-351 in Cliopatria: 797,305 km2, bbox 74.36-91.66E 20.02-27.67N, 3,069 cells. Of those cells 1,251 are Cliopatria's Haryanka land and 56 more its Avanti, Vatsa and Cedi discs, but about 1,800 more lie outside all of those (758 in Madhya Pradesh, 365 in Bangladesh, 163 in Uttar Pradesh, 155 in Chhattisgarh, 140 in Odisha, 72 in West Bengal and 63 in Rajasthan) and no page opened places the Shaishunagas there, although part of the Madhya Pradesh cells is the real Malwa and Narmada country of Avanti, which the corrected shape takes from the Avanti hand-over; the Shishunaga page gives the conquests only as 'He destroyed Pradyota dynasty of Avanti and conquered kingdoms of Kosala and Vatsa' and the dynasty page as 'annexing Avanti into Magadha' with 'one of the largest empires in the Indian subcontinent'. The corrected shape is the page-supported minimum, about 1,964 cells (497,000 km2, ratio 0.62 to Cliopatria): the Haryanka land plus Avanti with Vatsa, using the hand-over regions of the sibling dossiers. Kosala was already in the Haryanka land. The Shaishunaga land of Bengal, Odisha and Chhattisgarh in Cliopatria is dropped: the Nanda page puts 'Odisha in the east' and a Kalinga canal under the Nandas, not the Shaishunagas. Cliopatria's span begins 9 years late (-404 against 413). The page gives no area and its only map caption reads 'Approximate extent of the Shaishunaga dynasty', so there is no infobox figure to compare.

ledger.note: 413 BCE: Shishunaga takes the Magadhan throne after a popular rebellion and founds the Shaishunaga dynasty at Rajgir. Infobox 'Established: 413 BCE'; the Shishunaga page has 'He was placed on the throne by the people who revolted against the Haryanka dynasty rule'. The page gives the founding, not the land: the region is the Haryanka dossier's hand-over.

region.text: Avanti (Malwa and the Narmada country at Mahishmati) with Vatsa, as janapada-of-avanti hands it over: 'Shishunaga ended the Pradyota dynasty of Avanti'

ledger.note: 404 BCE: Magadha annexes Avanti and Vatsa. 'He conquered Avanti kingdom by defeating Nandivardhana or Avantivardhana, the last king of Pradyota dynasty' and 'He destroyed Pradyota dynasty of Avanti and conquered kingdoms of Kosala and Vatsa'. Page silent on the year: Shishunaga reigned 'c. 413 – c. 395 BCE'; -404 is the first year of Cliopatria's Shaishunaga shape, which holds the whole Avanti disc, and the Avanti dossier ends in -405 with this state as successor. Kosala is already in the Haryanka land, so no separate Kosala gain is drawn.

395 BCE: the capital moves to Pataliputra. 'but later shifted to Pataliputra, near the present day Patna, during the reign of Kalashoka'; the infobox lists his reign from 395 BCE. Page silent on the year of the move (it also credits 'the final transfer of the capital to Pataliputra' to Shishunaga), so -395 is the start of Kalashoka's reign; the Shishunaga page instead has the capital shifted to Vaishali.

ledger.note: 350 BCE: Matsya joins Magadha. 'This dynasty was succeeded by the Nanda dynasty in c. 345 BCE'; 'Mahanandin was killed by Mahapadma, his illegitimate son' (infobox 'Disestablished: 345 BCE'). wars.name: Revolt against the Haryanka dynasty
wars.outcome: The rebels place Shishunaga on the throne; no land changes hands beyond the change of dynasty.
wars.note: 'He was placed on the throne by the people who revolted against the Haryanka dynasty rule'; the dynasty page says he 'ascended to the throne after a popular rebellion in c. 413 BCE'. A change of dynasty, not a territorial war.

wars.name: Shishunaga's conquest of Avanti

zones.text: Avanti (Malwa and the Narmada country at Mahishmati) with Vatsa, as janapada-of-avanti hands it over: 'Shishunaga ended the Pradyota dynasty of Avanti'

wars.outcome: Magadha wins: Shishunaga defeats Nandivardhana (Avantivardhana), the last king of the Pradyota dynasty, and annexes Avanti; the page adds Kosala and Vatsa.
wars.note: Undated: the years are Shishunaga's reign ('c. 413 – c. 395 BCE'). No contest events are in the ledger because neither page dates a campaign or a battle; the annexation is the -404 gain (confidence 1).

wars.name: Mahapadma's seizure of the throne
wars.outcome: Mahapadma, called the illegitimate son of Mahanandin, kills him and founds the Nanda dynasty.
wars.note: 'Mahanandin was killed by Mahapadma, his illegitimate son'; the Buddhist tradition on the page has the ten sons 'ousted by Ugrasena Nanda'. A palace coup within one state, so no zone.

certainty.note: All frontiers are approximate: the only map on the page is captioned 'Approximate extent of the Shaishunaga dynasty' and the text gives no boundary; the Ganga, Son and Champa lines of the Magadhan core in the Haryanka dossier are the firmest, the Malwa and Matsya edges the softest.

notes: Budget: two pages for four shapes. START AND END: Cliopatria runs the row -404..-334; the pages give 413..345 (infobox), so the dossier starts in 413 (new keyframe -413..-405 closing the gap left by the Haryanka dossier, which ends in 413) and ends in 345 with the Nanda founding; the last Cliopatria shape (-337..-334) is verdict wrong for this slug and its years are carried by nanda-empire_-345. THE SHAPE: Cliopatria's three Shaishunaga shapes are one identical 797,305 km2 polygon (3,069 cells); it holds the Haryanka land, the Avanti, Vatsa and Cedi discs and some 1,800 further cells (Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Bangladesh) that neither page supports, and none of Matsya. I replaced it with the hand-over regions of the sibling dossiers (Haryanka's -413 dissolve, Avanti's successor land, Matsya's dissolve), so the three dossiers agree cell for cell; if a sibling's region changes, this dossier's regions must be re-copied. The corrected shape is the page-supported minimum and may be too small: the dynasty page says only 'ruled one of the largest empires in the Indian subcontinent'. NOT USED: Asmaka, which janapada-of-asmaka hands to this state in -345; neither page names it, and neither Cliopatria shape contains the Asmaka disc, so no event is written (the Nanda page has an undated Ashmaka theory). Kosala: the Shishunaga page says he 'conquered kingdoms of Kosala and Vatsa'; the Haryanka dossier already holds the Kosala land at -413, so only Vatsa (with Avanti) is a gain. DISAGREEMENTS: the capital (Rajgir, Vaishali, Pataliputra in different sentences of the two pages; the Haryanka page, per the sibling dossier, puts Pataliputra under Udayin around -460); the reign lists (infobox reigns against Puranic, Buddhist and Sarao dates); the date of the dynasty end (413/425 for its start on other pages). The Haryanka/Shaishunaga chronology here is the long one of the infobox; the short chronology puts everything about 90 years later. Gazetteer names wanted: Maheshwar (place, Narmada, about 22.18N 75.59E, copied from the Avanti hand-over region), Vaishali (place, about 25.99N 85.13E).
